course_title: Practical Exercise on European and Global Legal History
title: Exercise class 9: the Historical School, the jurisprudence of purpose, imperialism

slides.title: Why the Historical School arose: the need for calm after the revolutions
slides.text: The exercise class gives the Historical School a motive that textbooks often leave out, and it is the best explanation of its success. AFTER THE 'AGE OF REVOLUTIONS' (1776–1848/49) CAME A GENERAL NEED FOR STABILITY AND CALM, visible in the movement of HISTORICISM. And the culprit was named: NATURAL-LAW DOCTRINE, THAT IS, THE CONCEPTION OF NATURAL LAW AS A 'LAW OF REASON' BOUND UP WITH THE ENLIGHTENMENT, WAS BLAMED FOR THE REVOLUTIONS OF 1789, 1830 AND 1848. The Historical School is therefore not merely a scholarly programme — it is a POLITICAL ANSWER TO THE FEAR OF REVOLUTION. Whoever says that law GROWS GRADUALLY out of the spirit of the nation is at the same time saying that it IS NOT TO BE MADE ALL AT ONCE AND FROM ABOVE. IN 1814 CARL FRIEDRICH VON SAVIGNY (1779–1861, Berlin) published 'ON THE VOCATION OF OUR AGE FOR LEGISLATION AND JURISPRUDENCE', and THE HISTORICAL SCHOOL OF LAW DEVELOPED AS THE EXAMPLE OF NORM PRODUCTION THROUGH LEGAL SCHOLARSHIP — that is, as the third model. It is a COUNTER-MOVEMENT both to the codification movement and to the law of reason, and it derives law from the 'SPIRIT OF THE NATION' (VOLKSGEIST).

cards.q: What political motive lies behind the Historical School?
cards.a: After the 'AGE OF REVOLUTIONS' (1776–1848/49) came a GENERAL NEED FOR STABILITY AND CALM (the movement of HISTORICISM), and NATURAL-LAW DOCTRINE AS A 'LAW OF REASON' WAS BLAMED FOR THE REVOLUTIONS OF 1789, 1830 AND 1848. The school is therefore not merely a scholarly programme but a POLITICAL ANSWER TO THE FEAR OF REVOLUTION: whoever says law GROWS GRADUALLY says at the same time that it IS NOT TO BE MADE ALL AT ONCE AND FROM ABOVE.

slides.title: The method and its fruits: how the 'legal person' came about
slides.text: THE METHOD: HISTORICAL-SYSTEMATIC. The school RETURNED TO THE 'HISTORICAL SOURCES', SOUGHT TO IDENTIFY INDIVIDUAL LEGAL FIGURES AND TRACED HOW THOSE FIGURES DEVELOPED OVER TIME. THE GOAL: TO DETERMINE LEGAL PRINCIPLES, TO CREATE LEGAL CONCEPTS AND TO BRING THEM INTO A UNIFIED SYSTEM. And the exercise gives concrete fruits which show that this was not mere theory: IN THE SECOND HALF OF THE 19TH CENTURY CONCEPTS SUCH AS THE 'LEGAL PERSON' (JURISTISCHE PERSON) AND 'CAPACITY TO CONTRACT' (GESCHÄFTSFÄHIGKEIT) CAME INTO BEING. These are concepts we regard today as self-evident and without which no lawyer can work — and yet they are the creations of one scholarly school, barely a hundred and fifty years old. TWO CURRENTS WITHIN THE SCHOOL: PANDECTISM and GERMANISM.

cards.q: What method and goal did the Historical School have, and which concepts did it create?
cards.a: THE HISTORICAL-SYSTEMATIC METHOD: a return to the HISTORICAL SOURCES, the identification of INDIVIDUAL LEGAL FIGURES and the tracing of how they developed over time. THE GOAL: TO DETERMINE PRINCIPLES, CREATE CONCEPTS AND BRING THEM INTO A UNIFIED SYSTEM. The fruits: in the second half of the 19th century the concepts of the 'LEGAL PERSON' and 'CAPACITY TO CONTRACT' came into being — self-evident today, and yet barely a hundred and fifty years old.

slides.title: Begriffsjurisprudenz: who coined the name, and as an insult
slides.text: THE HISTORICAL SCHOOL OF LAW (PANDECTISM) GRADUALLY TURNED INTO 'CONCEPTUAL JURISPRUDENCE' (BEGRIFFSJURISPRUDENZ). And here is a detail to remember, because it is a typical exam question: THE TERM WAS COINED BY RUDOLF VON JHERING, AND AS A LABEL FOR THE THEORETICAL EXCESS IN CONCEPT-FORMATION of which, in his view, Pandectism was guilty in the form practised by GEORG FRIEDRICH PUCHTA (1798–1846) AND BERNHARD WINDSCHEID. It is therefore not the school's name for itself but A CRITICAL LABEL FROM AN APOSTATE. PUCHTA'S CONSTRUCTION: he worked with SCHELLING'S 'DOUBLE RATIONALITY' — HE SOUGHT TO FIND POSITIVE LAW BY HISTORICAL INVESTIGATION (Schelling's positive philosophy) AND AT THE SAME TIME TO UNDERSTAND IT AS A SYSTEM. It is precisely that combination of two routes — history and system — that allows the claim that new norms can be deduced from concepts; and it is precisely this that Jhering will turn against.

cards.q: Who coined the term 'Begriffsjurisprudenz' and in what sense?
cards.a: RUDOLF VON JHERING, as a LABEL FOR THE THEORETICAL EXCESS IN CONCEPT-FORMATION of which, in his view, PANDECTISM was guilty in the form practised by PUCHTA (1798–1846) AND WINDSCHEID. It is NOT the school's name for itself but A CRITICAL LABEL FROM AN APOSTATE.
cards.topic: Constitutionalism & Norm Production III; Legal Education and Legal Professions

slides.title: The BGB as the school's fruit — with its flaw
slides.text: THE 'RESULT' OF THE HISTORICAL SCHOOL OF LAW IS THE GERMAN CIVIL CODIFICATION (BGB), WHICH CAME INTO FORCE ON 1 JANUARY 1900. It rests ON THE SYSTEMATIZATION OF THE HISTORICAL SCHOOL, that is, on conceptual jurisprudence, and HAS THE PANDECTIST STRUCTURE. THE FIRST DRAFT WAS PREPARED BY THE LEGAL SCHOLAR OTTO FRIEDRICH VON GIERKE (famous for German law of associations). And the exercise adds a criticism that is useful in the exam, because it shows the price of that method: BECAUSE OF ITS HIGH ABSTRACTION AND BECAUSE IT IS A PRODUCT OF THE ACADEMIC WORLD, THE BGB IS VERY HARD FOR THE ORDINARY CITIZEN TO READ. Compare the ABGB, which was written so that even the uneducated could understand it — one of the basic demands of an Enlightenment codification was INTELLIGIBILITY. The Pandectist codification SACRIFICED THAT DEMAND TO PRECISION AND SYSTEM. That is the concrete price of the third model: LAW MADE BY SCHOLARSHIP IS PRECISE BUT CEASES TO BE ACCESSIBLE TO THOSE IT IS MEANT TO SERVE.

cards.q: What is the price of the Pandectist method, as shown by the BGB?
cards.a: The BGB rests on the SYSTEMATIZATION OF THE HISTORICAL SCHOOL and has the PANDECTIST STRUCTURE, but BECAUSE OF ITS HIGH ABSTRACTION AND ACADEMIC ORIGIN IT IS VERY HARD FOR THE ORDINARY CITIZEN TO READ. The Enlightenment codification (the ABGB) demanded INTELLIGIBILITY — the Pandectist one SACRIFICED IT TO PRECISION AND SYSTEM. LAW MADE BY SCHOLARSHIP IS PRECISE BUT CEASES TO BE ACCESSIBLE.

slides.title: Jhering's turn: from the cult of logic to the question 'why?'
slides.text: IN THE MIDDLE OF THE 19TH CENTURY RUDOLF VON JHERING TURNS AWAY FROM PUCHTA AND THE HISTORICAL SCHOOL, WHICH HE ACCUSES OF 'CONCEPTUAL JURISPRUDENCE'. The exercise class sums up his programme in three rejections and one question. HE REJECTS THE 'CULT OF LOGIC'. HE REJECTS THE 'DELUSION OF A MATHEMATICS OF LAW'. AND HE CLAIMS THAT LEGAL QUESTIONS ARE TO BE SOLVED AS QUESTIONS OF EXPEDIENCY (ZWECKMÄSSIGKEITSFRAGEN). THE JUSTIFICATION IS ELEGANT: BECAUSE LAW, ON JHERING'S VIEW, HAS THE FORM OF A COMMAND, THE QUESTION 'WHY?' MUST ALWAYS STAND AT THE CENTRE OF ATTENTION AND INTERPRETATION — that is, THE QUESTION OF PURPOSE IN LAW. Whoever commands, commands towards something; and an interpreter who does not know that purpose cannot understand the command. WITH HIS 'JURISPRUDENCE OF PURPOSE' JHERING INAUGURATES MODERN LEGAL SCHOLARSHIP — the exercise stresses this with three exclamation marks, and it is worth remembering as a turning point: FROM JHERING ON, LAW ASKS NOT ONLY 'WHAT FOLLOWS FROM THE CONCEPT' BUT 'WHAT IS IT FOR'. In the second half of the 19th century LEGAL POSITIVISM also gains ground.

terms.def: Jhering's programme: legal questions are questions of expediency; because law has the form of a command, one must ask 'why?'.

cards.q: What does Jhering reject and what does he put at the centre?
cards.a: He rejects the 'CULT OF LOGIC' and the 'DELUSION OF A MATHEMATICS OF LAW' and claims that LEGAL QUESTIONS ARE TO BE SOLVED AS QUESTIONS OF EXPEDIENCY. The justification: BECAUSE LAW HAS THE FORM OF A COMMAND, THE QUESTION 'WHY?' MUST STAND AT THE CENTRE OF INTERPRETATION — the QUESTION OF PURPOSE. With his JURISPRUDENCE OF PURPOSE he INAUGURATES MODERN LEGAL SCHOLARSHIP.
cards.topic: Constitutionalism & Norm Production III; Legal Education and Legal Professions

slides.title: What grew out of the jurisprudence of purpose
slides.text: The exercise class gives the whole tree of successors, which is useful for a question about the development of method. THE JURISPRUDENCE OF PURPOSE IS THE BASIS FOR: (1) THE JURISPRUDENCE OF INTERESTS (INTERESSENJURISPRUDENZ), developed at the beginning of the 20th century by PHILIPP HECK; (2) ALL KINDS OF 'SOCIOLOGICAL JURISPRUDENCE'; (3) THE FREE LAW MOVEMENT (FREIRECHTSBEWEGUNG) — EUGEN EHRLICH, HERMANN KANTOROWICZ, ERNST FUCHS — whose aim is TO REDUCE THE JUDGE'S BINDING TO THE STATUTE IN FAVOUR OF JUDICIAL DISCRETION. AND THE OVERSEAS BRANCH: IN THE USA THE 'SEARCH FOR PURPOSE IN LAW' IS MIRRORED AT THE BEGINNING OF THE 20TH CENTURY IN THE WORK OF ROSCOE POUND AND IN HIS VERSION OF 'SOCIOLOGICAL JURISPRUDENCE'. With that the circle closes back to what you know from Kennedy: this current is precisely 'THE SOCIAL' of the second globalization. Jhering's question 'why?' thus leads in the end from a German chair to American reform legislation.

cards.q: What grew out of Jhering's jurisprudence of purpose?
cards.a: 1) THE JURISPRUDENCE OF INTERESTS (PHILIPP HECK, early 20th century). 2) All kinds of SOCIOLOGICAL JURISPRUDENCE. 3) THE FREE LAW MOVEMENT (EHRLICH, KANTOROWICZ, FUCHS), which seeks TO REDUCE THE JUDGE'S BINDING TO THE STATUTE IN FAVOUR OF JUDICIAL DISCRETION. And in the USA the 'search for purpose' is mirrored in ROSCOE POUND — precisely what Kennedy calls 'THE SOCIAL'.

slides.title: Source: Art. 1 of the Swiss ZGB
slides.text: THE SOURCE: '1. The law applies according to its wording or interpretation to all legal questions for which it contains a provision. 2. IN THE ABSENCE OF A PROVISION, THE COURT SHALL DECIDE IN ACCORDANCE WITH CUSTOMARY LAW AND, IN THE ABSENCE OF CUSTOMARY LAW, IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE RULE THAT IT WOULD MAKE AS LEGISLATOR. 3. In doing so, the court follows established doctrine and case law.' This article is the most famous provision in all of comparative private law and deserves careful reading. THE THIRD PARAGRAPH IS AS IMPORTANT AS THE SECOND: the judge may indeed decide 'as legislator', but NOT ARBITRARILY — he is bound by DOCTRINE AND CASE LAW. It is therefore freedom within the discipline, not outside it. THE SWISS ZGB, WRITTEN BY EUGEN HUBER, DATES FROM 1907. IT STANDS IN THE TRADITION OF THE HISTORICAL SCHOOL (like the BGB), BUT DEVELOPS IT FURTHER: IT NO LONGER FOLLOWS THE IDEA OF COMPLETENESS. The traditional Historical School held to the idea of the COMPLETENESS OF THE LEGAL ORDER, that is, that it CONTAINS NO GAPS — and the ZGB abandons that assumption. THE JUDGE BECOMES MORE POWERFUL IN THE ZGB, exactly as the quoted provision shows. FOR A LONG TIME IT WAS REGARDED AS THE MOST PROGRESSIVE CODIFICATION IN THE WORLD — AND AFTER THE FIRST WORLD WAR IT WAS ADOPTED BY TURKEY UNDER KEMAL ATATÜRK.

cards.q: What does Art. 1 of the Swiss ZGB provide and why does its third paragraph matter?
cards.a: In the absence of a provision the court decides ACCORDING TO CUSTOMARY LAW, and in its absence ACCORDING TO THE RULE IT WOULD MAKE AS LEGISLATOR. The third paragraph matters just as much: IN DOING SO IT FOLLOWS ESTABLISHED DOCTRINE AND CASE LAW — the judge may decide 'as legislator' but NOT ARBITRARILY. It is FREEDOM WITHIN THE DISCIPLINE, NOT OUTSIDE IT.

cards.q: How does the ZGB develop the Historical School further, and who adopted it?
cards.a: It was written by EUGEN HUBER (1907); it stands in the school's tradition but NO LONGER FOLLOWS THE IDEA OF COMPLETENESS — the traditional school held that the legal order CONTAINS NO GAPS, and the ZGB abandons that; THE JUDGE THEREBY BECOMES MORE POWERFUL. It was long regarded as the MOST PROGRESSIVE CODIFICATION IN THE WORLD and AFTER THE FIRST WORLD WAR IT WAS ADOPTED BY TURKEY UNDER ATATÜRK.

slides.title: Eugen Ehrlich and living law from Bukovina
slides.text: EUGEN EHRLICH (1862–1922) is a particularly rewarding figure for this course, because his theory grew out of a concrete place. AROUND 1903 HE BEGAN WORKING ON A CONCEPTION OF THE LEGAL ORDER THAT WOULD TAKE MORE ACCOUNT OF LEGAL REALITY. And the exercise says exactly what prompted him: HIS OBSERVATION OF LEGAL REALITY IN BUKOVINA, WHICH WAS ETHNICALLY VERY DIVERSE, LED HIM TO PAY MORE ATTENTION TO 'LIVING LAW'. Bukovina was the easternmost crown land of the monarchy, where Ruthenians, Romanians, Germans, Jews, Poles and Armenians lived side by side — and Ehrlich saw that what people actually governed themselves by did not coincide with the Austrian code. THE CONCLUSION: since, according to his sociological studies, POSITIVE LAW CANNOT IN THE END PRODUCE COMPLETE JUSTICE, HE SHIFTED THE CENTRE OF GRAVITY TO THE PERSON OF THE JUDGE, WHO — RELATIVELY INDEPENDENTLY OF THE STATUTE, SINCE SEVERAL COURTS MAY REACH DIFFERENT DECISIONS IN THE SAME MATTER — DOES NOT FIND JUSTICE BUT CREATES IT HIMSELF. IN THIS RESPECT EHRLICH IS THE FOUNDER OF THE SO-CALLED FREE LAW MOVEMENT. Note the route by which this was reached: FROM THE OBSERVATION OF A MULTI-ETHNIC PROVINCE TO THE CLAIM THAT THE JUDGE CREATES LAW.

cards.q: What led Ehrlich to the concept of 'living law'?
cards.a: HIS OBSERVATION OF LEGAL REALITY IN BUKOVINA, WHICH WAS ETHNICALLY VERY DIVERSE (Ruthenians, Romanians, Germans, Jews, Poles, Armenians) — he saw that WHAT PEOPLE ACTUALLY GOVERNED THEMSELVES BY DID NOT COINCIDE WITH THE AUSTRIAN CODE. Around 1903 he began working on a conception of law that would take more account of LEGAL REALITY.
cards.topic: Constitutionalism & Norm Production III; Legal Education and Legal Professions

cards.q: What conclusion about the judge did Ehrlich reach?
cards.a: Since POSITIVE LAW CANNOT PRODUCE COMPLETE JUSTICE, he shifted the centre of gravity to the PERSON OF THE JUDGE, WHO — relatively independently of the statute, since SEVERAL COURTS MAY REACH DIFFERENT DECISIONS IN THE SAME MATTER — DOES NOT FIND JUSTICE BUT CREATES IT HIMSELF. Hence he is the founder of the FREE LAW MOVEMENT.
cards.topic: Constitutionalism & Norm Production III; Legal Education and Legal Professions

slides.title: The universalization of law and the three kinds of humanity
slides.text: The exercise class explains the 'European century' through law and gives it a sharp conclusion. IT IS THE 'EUROPEAN CENTURY' BECAUSE EUROPEAN LAW, VALUES AND IDEAS SPREAD ACROSS THE WHOLE WORLD — this is called the 'UNIVERSALIZATION' OF INTERNATIONAL LAW IN THE 19TH CENTURY. And the exercise adds a connection that is surprising and good: THE RISE OF POSITIVISM MAKES IT POSSIBLE TO OVERCOME THE EXCLUSION OF NON-CHRISTIAN SUBJECTS FROM INTERNATIONAL LAW. For as long as international law was derived from Christian natural law, a non-Christian could not belong to it; once it rests on THE CONSENT OF STATES, anyone can consent. Positivism therefore paradoxically opened the door. BUT THE RESULT IS TWOFOLD: EQUALITY IS THE GUIDING PRINCIPLE FOR RELATIONS BETWEEN THE EUROPEAN POWERS — BUT IN RELATIONS BETWEEN EUROPEAN AND NON-EUROPEAN COUNTRIES INEQUALITY APPLIES. And that inequality was given a conceptual form one must know, because it is among the harshest evidence of the thinking of the age: THREE KINDS OF HUMANITY WERE DISTINGUISHED — 'CIVILIZED HUMANITY', 'BARBARIAN HUMANITY' (SEMI-CIVILIZED) AND 'SAVAGE HUMANITY'. On the classification depended whether the entity in question was a subject of international law, whether equal treaties could be concluded with it, or whether its territory could be treated as terra nullius.

cards.q: Why did positivism paradoxically open international law to non-Christians?
cards.a: Because as long as international law was derived from CHRISTIAN NATURAL LAW, a non-Christian could not belong to it; once it rests on THE CONSENT OF STATES, ANYONE CAN CONSENT. THE RISE OF POSITIVISM THEREFORE MADE IT POSSIBLE TO OVERCOME THE EXCLUSION OF NON-CHRISTIAN SUBJECTS.

cards.q: Which three kinds of humanity were distinguished in the 19th century and why did it matter?
cards.a: 'CIVILIZED HUMANITY', 'BARBARIAN HUMANITY' (SEMI-CIVILIZED) AND 'SAVAGE HUMANITY'. It mattered because on the classification depended WHETHER THE ENTITY WAS A SUBJECT OF INTERNATIONAL LAW, whether EQUAL TREATIES could be concluded with it, or whether its territory could be treated as TERRA NULLIUS. EQUALITY applied among European powers, INEQUALITY in relations with non-European countries.

slides.title: Two models of European expansion
slides.text: The exercise class distinguishes TWO 'MODELS' OF LATE 19TH-CENTURY EUROPEAN EXPANSION, and the distinction is very useful for a question on colonialism. (1) THE FRENCH MODEL: EXPANSION BY FORMAL ARMIES, FOLLOWED BY COLONIAL OFFICIALS. The state goes first, trade follows. (2) THE ENGLISH AND GERMAN MODEL: THE ACQUISITION OF LAND BY PRIVATE AGENTS UNDER THE PROTECTION OF THE METROPOLITAN STATE, WHICH ONLY LATER TURNS INTO FORMAL COLONIES. Here a company or an individual goes first and the state legalizes afterwards what has already happened. The difference has large legal consequences: in the first case the title is public-law from the outset; in the second it derives from TREATIES CONCLUDED BY A PRIVATE PERSON WITH A LOCAL RULER — which is precisely why so many colonial titles rest on treaties of doubtful validity. AND EXTRATERRITORIALITY AS A THIRD FORM: CONSULAR JURISDICTION AND EXTRATERRITORIALITY FOR EUROPEAN TRADERS, AND THE LAW OF THE 'MOTHER COUNTRY' FOR SETTLERS. Law therefore travelled with the person, not with the territory — which is, incidentally, a return to the same personal conception of law as in early medieval Germanic law.

cards.q: Which two models of European expansion does the exercise class distinguish?
cards.a: 1) THE FRENCH: EXPANSION BY FORMAL ARMIES, followed by COLONIAL OFFICIALS — the state goes first. 2) THE ENGLISH AND GERMAN: THE ACQUISITION OF LAND BY PRIVATE AGENTS UNDER THE PROTECTION OF THE METROPOLITAN STATE, formal colonies only later — a company goes first and the state legalizes afterwards. In the second case the title derives from TREATIES OF A PRIVATE PERSON WITH A LOCAL RULER, which is why so many colonial titles are doubtful.

cards.q: How did extraterritoriality work and what is remarkable about it?
cards.a: CONSULAR JURISDICTION AND EXTRATERRITORIALITY FOR EUROPEAN TRADERS and the LAW OF THE 'MOTHER COUNTRY' FOR SETTLERS. What is remarkable is that LAW TRAVELLED WITH THE PERSON, NOT WITH THE TERRITORY — a return to the same PERSONAL CONCEPTION OF LAW as in early medieval Germanic law.

slides.title: The Berlin Conference: background, participants and effective occupation
slides.text: THE BACKGROUND according to the exercise class: THE EUROPEAN RACE FOR COLONIES LED GERMANY TO BEGIN SENDING OUT ITS OWN EXPEDITIONS, WHICH ALARMED BRITISH AND FRENCH STATESMEN. KING LEOPOLD II OF BELGIUM, HOPING TO CALM THE DISPUTE QUICKLY, PERSUADED FRANCE AND GERMANY THAT COMMON TRADE IN AFRICA WAS IN THE BEST INTEREST OF ALL THREE COUNTRIES. OTTO VON BISMARCK THEN, IN 1884, SUMMONED TO BERLIN REPRESENTATIVES OF THIRTEEN EUROPEAN NATIONS AND THE UNITED STATES TO WORK OUT A COMMON POLICY FOR THE AFRICAN CONTINENT. THE PARTICIPANTS according to the exercise: GREAT BRITAIN, FRANCE, SPAIN, THE NETHERLANDS, GERMANY, AUSTRIA-HUNGARY, RUSSIA, DENMARK, SWEDEN-NORWAY, THE OTTOMAN EMPIRE AND THE UNITED STATES. (The slide says the only African participant was the Congo — note this: it was the INTERNATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF THE CONGO, that is, Leopold II's private undertaking, not an African state; African political entities were not represented. In the exam keep to what the lecturer says, but it is useful to know the difference.) THE RESULTS IN INTERNATIONAL LAW: THE REGULATION OF FREE TRADE AND FREE NAVIGATION ON THE CONGO AND THE NIGER and A SET OF RULES FOR THE OCCUPATION OF TERRITORY, that is, THE 'PRINCIPLE OF EFFECTIVE OCCUPATION'. ART. 35 OF THE FINAL ACT provided that A POWER MAY ACQUIRE RIGHTS TO COLONIAL LANDS ONLY IF IT HOLDS THEM OR HAS EFFECTIVE OCCUPATION — which the exercise specifies by three features: IF IT HAS TREATIES WITH LOCAL LEADERS, IF IT HAS RAISED ITS FLAG THERE AND IF IT HAS ESTABLISHED AN ADMINISTRATION WITH A POLICE FORCE TO MAINTAIN ORDER. The power could also EXPLOIT THE COLONY ECONOMICALLY. AND THE SECOND, LESS WELL-KNOWN FUNCTION OF THAT PRINCIPLE: IT SERVED NOT ONLY TO ACQUIRE TERRITORIAL SOVEREIGNTY BUT ALSO TO DELIMIT THE BOUNDARIES BETWEEN THE OVERSEAS POSSESSIONS OF THE INDIVIDUAL POWERS — in some cases effective occupation became THE CRITERION FOR SETTLING COLONIAL BOUNDARY DISPUTES.

cards.q: What was the immediate background to the Berlin Conference?
cards.a: THE EUROPEAN RACE FOR COLONIES LED GERMANY TO SEND OUT ITS OWN EXPEDITIONS, which ALARMED THE BRITISH AND THE FRENCH. KING LEOPOLD II OF BELGIUM persuaded France and Germany that COMMON TRADE IN AFRICA was in the interest of all three — and BISMARCK then, in 1884, summoned to Berlin representatives of THIRTEEN EUROPEAN NATIONS AND THE USA.

cards.q: Which three features does effective occupation have under Art. 35?
cards.a: A power acquires rights to a colonial land only if it holds it or has EFFECTIVE OCCUPATION, that is: IT HAS TREATIES WITH LOCAL LEADERS, IT HAS RAISED ITS FLAG THERE and IT HAS ESTABLISHED AN ADMINISTRATION WITH A POLICE FORCE TO MAINTAIN ORDER. It could also EXPLOIT THE COLONY ECONOMICALLY.

cards.q: What second, less well-known function did the principle of effective occupation have?
cards.a: It served not only to ACQUIRE TERRITORIAL SOVEREIGNTY but also to DELIMIT THE BOUNDARIES BETWEEN THE OVERSEAS POSSESSIONS OF THE INDIVIDUAL POWERS — in some cases it became THE CRITERION FOR SETTLING COLONIAL BOUNDARY DISPUTES.
